theater: 福基斯北境克雷提庫姆谷地

battle.name: 佩爾狄卡斯三世
battle.theater: 福基斯北境克雷提庫姆谷地
battle.brief: 第三次聖戰期間，底比斯的埃帕米農達斯與佩爾狄卡斯率重裝步兵方陣侵入福基斯，在克雷提庫姆谷地與福基斯聯軍連戰三日，末段以縱深方陣迂迴，擊潰對手。卡面的斯巴達長矛正是底比斯方陣的骨幹：兩米長的梣木槍配鐵矛頭與青銅尾套，槍尖越過圓盾層層相接，撐起那面靠推力取勝的槍牆。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 第三次聖戰開打時，交戰的單位是城邦聯盟而不是國家。底比斯一方代表安菲克提翁同盟：議會判定福基斯違規之後，議決由最有勢力的成員底比斯出兵，實際戰務由底比斯將領埃帕米農達斯與佩爾狄卡斯主持，底比斯的執政官（Boetarch）議會決定是否開戰與兵額，兵員以底比斯重裝步兵為主，輔以玻俄提亞盟邦如塔納格拉、哈爾斯等城的人，以及帖薩利人提供的騎兵與輕步兵。底比斯最負盛名的單位是三百人的「神聖連隊」，由一百五十對伴侶組成，多為貴族青年，此役由佩爾狄卡斯直接統率，作為全軍的支點。福基斯一方是福基斯聯盟，由境內十餘座城邦各出民兵，組成以圓盾長矛為主的步兵方陣，戰時由聯盟議事會作最高決策，議會在克雷提庫姆一帶的城鎮開會；聯軍統帥斐洛梅洛斯於前356年自任將軍，此役仍在他任內，他要到前354年被刺身亡，帥印才交到俄諾馬科斯手上。第三方大致保持中立：斯巴達同情福基斯，卻正深陷自身困境而無力出兵；雅典在科林斯戰爭中與底比斯結盟，此役未有成建制部隊參戰；呂西安、亞卡迪亞諸邦亦未介入。
countriesEn: When the Third Sacred War broke out, the units that fought were federations of city-states rather than nations. The Theban side spoke for the Amphictyonic League: after the council had judged Phocis in violation of the rules, it resolved that the most powerful member, Thebes, would send the army, while the actual conduct of operations was directed by the Theban commanders Epaminondas and Pelopidas, and the council of the Theban magistrates (the Boetarchs) decided whether to go to war and at what strength. The troops were chiefly Theban hoplites, reinforced by men from the other Boeotian cities such as Tanagra and Haliartus, together with cavalry and light infantry supplied by the Thessalians. The most famous formation in the Theban army was the Sacred Band of three hundred men, a hundred and fifty pairs, largely drawn from the young nobility; in this campaign Pelopidas commanded it directly and it served as the fulcrum of the whole army. The Phocian side was the Phocian League, assembled from the militias of a dozen or more towns in the region into an infantry phalanx of round shields and spears; at the time supreme decision-making rested with the league council, which met in the towns around the Creticum. The commander of the federal army was Philomelus, who appointed himself strategos in 356 BC; this battle still falls within his tenure, and it was only after his assassination in 354 BC that the command passed to Onomarchus. The third parties largely stayed neutral: Sparta sympathised with Phocis but was too absorbed by its own troubles to send an army; Athens was allied with Thebes in the Corinthian War but committed no formed body to this campaign; and the peoples of Locris and Arcadia did not intervene at all.
people: 佩爾狄卡斯出身底比斯大族，青年時曾作為人質滯留斯巴達，回國後因被控謀反而受審，靠當場陳詞免罪，此後以膽識著稱。普魯塔克記他曾得「底比斯匕首」一類的兇名，說明他行事峻烈、不循常規；他與埃帕米農達斯恰好互補：埃帕米農達斯長於算計與縱深，佩爾狄卡斯長於親身帶鋒與強行突破。前371年留克特拉之戰，佩爾狄卡斯率神聖連隊在左翼投入，作為全軍支點；到這次三日之戰，他仍是底比斯最前線的指揮者之一，戰中腿部受創（依普魯塔克記載，創口包紮之後他仍留宿營中），卻沒有因此離開指揮位置。埃帕米農達斯在底比斯的聲望來自留克特拉，人稱「底比斯之獅」，此前曾兩度被放逐，據說是隱忍等待時機；這次他以將軍身分策劃越境作戰，對底比斯「先發制人」的政策有直接影響。福基斯方面的斐洛梅洛斯原是法爾薩拉斯的私人衛士首領，出身微賤而無門第，靠一次成功的奪取德爾斐站上檯面，成為聯盟名義上的領袖並發動聖戰。戰記細節主要來自戴奧多羅斯·西西里庫斯的《歷史叢書》第十六卷，另有保薩尼阿斯《希臘地誌》第九卷第十三節與普魯塔克《佩爾狄卡斯傳》互相對照。基層的關鍵人物則是各隊的「五十人長」與神聖連隊的百夫長：方陣的推進與停穩全靠他們的號令。
peopleEn: Pelopidas came from one of the great Theban families. As a young man he had been kept at Sparta as a hostage, and after his return he was put on trial for conspiracy and acquitted by the force of his own defence; from then on he was known for his nerve. Plutarch records that he earned a sobriquet of the Theban dagger, which shows how violently and by no ordinary rule he acted; he and Epaminondas complemented each other neatly, Epaminondas being the calculator of depth and Pelopidas the man who led from the front and forced a way through. At the battle of Leuctra in 371 BC Pelopidas threw the Sacred Band into the left wing as the fulcrum of the whole army; by the time of this three-day battle he was still one of the Theban commanders furthest forward, and he was wounded in the leg during the fighting (according to Plutarch the wound was dressed and he stayed in camp that night) without thereby leaving his post. Epaminondas's standing at Thebes came from Leuctra; he was called the Theban lion, and he had twice been exiled, it is said, in order to wait his moment with patience. In this campaign he planned the invasion as a general in his own right, and he had a direct hand in the Theban policy of striking first. On the Phocian side, Philomelus had been the commander of the private guard of Pharsalus; a man of low birth with no family backing, he rose to prominence by a single successful seizure of Delphi, became the nominal leader of the league and launched the sacred war. The most detailed account of the fighting comes from the sixteenth book of Diodorus Siculus' Bibliotheca Historica, checked against Pausanias, Description of Greece 9.13, and Plutarch's Life of Pelopidas. At the lower levels the decisive men were the file leaders of the fifty and the captains of the Sacred Band: the advance and the halt of a phalanx depended entirely on their orders.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛（dory）正是本役的骨幹兵器：一根約兩米長的梣木或白蠟木桿，前端裝葉形鐵矛頭，後端套一枚青銅矛尾，槍身常刻各城邦的名號與守護神徽記；尾套的實用功能是插地支撐身體、掩護後排預備的槍，也避免槍尾在地面的磨損傷到矛尖。作戰中它不用來擲——dory 的重心與配重都不利投擲——而是拿來「推」：重裝步兵一手持圓盾、一手執槍，槍尖越過盾緣刺向前方身體，槍桿被前排身體遮住的部分則由後排越過自己人肩頭刺出，這正是縱深方陣的技術前提。埃帕米農達斯的方陣把後排槍尖層層疊在前排頭頂之上，槍牆的厚度就是陣線的厚度。配套裝備方面，重裝步兵另有科林斯式青銅頭盔、圓盾（aspis）、護脛、青銅鱗甲或亞麻胸甲；短劍（xiphos）只在長矛被格擋時用來劈砍。戴奧多羅斯記載，底比斯人此役改用亞麻胸甲，因福基斯人的銳器難以刺穿，被視為底比斯能在平原上僵持的助力之一。遠程火力由弓箭手與投石索手提供，帖薩利與馬其頓式騎兵擔任追擊與包抄。此役是三日野戰而非攻城，沒有投石機、攻城塔或撞槌一類器械參與；後勤也相對簡單：重裝步兵自備數日口糧與盾牌，沿福基斯邊境的道路行軍，飲水取自當地溪流，傷兵則退往最近的城邑。
kitsEn: The dory on the card is precisely the backbone weapon of this campaign: a shaft of ash or lime wood about two metres long, fitted with a leaf-shaped iron head at the front and a bronze butt-spike at the rear, and often marked with the name and the patron deity of the issuing polis. The practical function of the butt-spike was to plant the spear in the ground to support the body, to cover the spears held in reserve by the rear ranks, and to keep the butt from being abraded on the ground in a way that would spoil the head. In battle it was not thrown: the balance and the weight of a dory make it a poor javelin. It was used to push. A hoplite carried a round shield in one hand and the spear in the other, the point reaching past the rim of the shield at the body of the enemy, and the part of the shaft hidden by the body of the man in front was driven by the rear rank over the shoulders of his own comrades. That is the technical precondition for a deep phalanx. Epaminondas' formation stacked the points of the rear ranks above the heads of those in front, so that the thickness of the wall of spears was the thickness of the line. As for the rest of the panoply, the hoplite had a Corinthian bronze helmet, a round shield (aspis), greaves, and a bronze or linen cuirass; the short sword (xiphos) was used only to cut and slash once the spear had been checked. Diodorus records that the Thebans used linen cuirasses in this campaign, so that the sharp weapons of the Phocians could not pierce them, and this is treated as one of the reasons the Thebans could hold on in the open plain. Ranged fire was supplied by archers and slingers, while Thessalian and Macedonian-style cavalry performed the pursuit and the outflanking. This was a three-day field battle rather than a siege, and no artillery, siege tower or battering ram took part; the logistics were correspondingly simple. The hoplites carried their own rations for several days along with their shields, marched by the roads along the Phocidian border, drew water from the local streams, and sent the wounded back to the nearest towns.
tactics: 底比斯軍的戰術起點是一次越境遠征：聯軍自底比斯出發，經克雷提庫姆一帶的山口進入福基斯西部平原，先以騎兵與輕步兵遮蔽行軍縱隊，搜索福基斯人集結的方向，兩軍在谷地狹窄處遭遇後就地展開。第一日，雙方列陣相持：底比斯人沒有強攻，而是以密集的槍陣試探對手，接戰以標槍與箭矢互射，陣線在平原上反覆推移，誰也未能取得決定性優勢——這一日的收穫是底比斯人摸清了福基斯陣地的地形與縱深。第二日，底比斯人奪取有利地形，把福基斯人從原先據守的位置擠開，穩住陣腳。第三日才是決戰：底比斯集中所部的精兵，以左翼縱深與迂迴的思路壓向福基斯陣線的側後，福基斯方陣在僵持中被突破，全軍當場潰散，底比斯的騎兵與輕步兵隨即追擊，把潰兵一直趕到福基斯境內與山區的交界。整場戰役的特點是「打位置」而不是「打一擊」：底比斯連打三日，以每日一點進展換取最後的側翼條件，再用一擊定勝負。史料沒有留下此役的縱深排數，五十排這類說法只適用於前371年的留克特拉；但可以確定的是，底比斯延續了以精兵深縱、翼側拒止的部署思路，把最重的一擊留到地形與士氣都站在自己這邊的時候。福基斯方面的應對則以守勢對抗：步兵密集結陣、以長矛封住正面，等待底比斯自行消耗，結果在陣線被側翼突破之後失去縱深，全軍一潰而散。連日作戰同樣考驗後勤：糧食須由鄰近城鎮輸送，傷兵向後方城邑撤退，神聖連隊因編制小、士氣高而始終留在陣中未曾拆散。
tacticsEn: The tactical premise of the Theban army was an invasion across the border. The coalition marched out of Thebes, came through the passes around the Creticum into the western plain of Phocis, screened the marching column with cavalry and light infantry, and searched for the direction in which the Phocians were assembling; the two armies met where the valley narrowed and there deployed on the spot. On the first day the two sides stood in formation and held each other: the Thebans did not assault but probed the enemy with a dense front of spears, the exchange was by javelin and arrow, and the line was pushed back and forth across the plain without any decisive advantage for either man — the gain of that first day was that the Thebans learned the ground and the depth of the Phocian position. On the second day the Thebans took the favourable ground, squeezed the Phocians out of the positions they had held and settled their own footing. The third day was the decisive one. The Thebans concentrated their best troops and pressed against the flank and rear of the Phocian line in the manner of the deep left wing and the turning movement; the Phocian phalanx was broken in the stalemate and the whole army collapsed on the spot, and Theban cavalry and light infantry pursued the rout as far as the border between the Phocidian interior and the mountains. The character of the whole engagement was positional rather than a single blow: Thebes fought for three days, buying the conditions for the final flanking move one day's step at a time, and then settled it in one stroke. The sources give no figure for the depth of the formation in this battle; the famous fifty ranks apply only to Leuctra in 371 BC. What is certain is that the Thebes carried over the approach of concentrating the best troops in depth and refusing the flank, holding back the heaviest stroke until both the ground and the morale were on their side. The Phocians met it defensively: their infantry closed up in a dense line and sealed the front with their spears, waiting for the Thebans to exhaust themselves, and when the line was turned they had no depth left and the whole army dissolved in a single rout. Fighting on successive days also strained logistics: grain had to be brought up from the neighbouring towns, the wounded were carried back to the towns behind the line, and the Sacred Band, small in numbers and high in spirit, was never broken up and stayed in the line throughout.
data: 這場戰役留下的數字不多，可以確定的是以下幾項。第一，戰役分三日進行，這在希臘戰爭史中是罕見的長時間會戰，兩軍連續三天都在野外列陣交鋒。第二，底比斯方面的神聖連隊定編三百人，即一百五十對伴侶，這支部隊在此役中沒有被拆散投入全面消耗，而是作為全軍支點使用。第三，雙方兵力沒有留下可信的數字；一般認為底比斯方面的重裝步兵在數千人，加上玻俄提亞盟邦與帖薩利騎兵，總數可達萬人上下，福基斯方面則由各城民兵湊成，規模相近，兩軍在紙面上並不懸殊。第四，作為對照，前371年留克特拉之戰底比斯方面的重裝步兵約六千至七千，斯巴達及其盟友合計約一萬人，可看出底比斯當年是以少打多的傳統打法。第五，地理上戰場在福基斯北境克雷提庫姆谷地，靠近今阿姆菲薩（Amfissa）一帶，底比斯城至此直線約八十公里，道路則須翻越山口，沿途沒有大型補給點。第六，此役繫於前356年夏，第三次聖戰自此爆發，一直打到前346年才由馬其頓介入而終結，前後約十年。第七，同年七月廿一日以弗所的阿耳忒彌斯神廟焚於大火，希臘人視為國運之凶兆，恰好落在底比斯連勝的年份裡。至於傷亡數字，兩造均無可信記載，只能說福基斯聯軍的野戰部隊幾乎全滅，底比斯的損失相對輕微。
dataEn: This campaign has left few figures, and the following are the ones that can be stated with confidence. First, the battle was fought over three days, which makes it a rare long engagement in Greek military history: both armies were formed up and fighting in the open field on three consecutive days. Second, the Theban Sacred Band was established at three hundred men, that is a hundred and fifty pairs, and in this campaign the unit was not broken up and thrown into general attrition but used as the fulcrum of the whole army. Third, no reliable figures survive for the size of either force. The Theban hoplites are usually reckoned in the low thousands, and with the men of the Boeotian cities and the Thessalian cavalry the total on the Theban side is put at around ten thousand, while the Phocian side was assembled from the militias of the individual towns and was of comparable size, so that on paper the two armies were not mismatched. Fourth, by way of comparison, at Leuctra in 371 BC the Theban hoplites numbered about six to seven thousand against roughly ten thousand for Sparta and its allies, which shows the tradition of Thebes fighting outnumbered. Fifth, geographically the battlefield lay in the valley of the Creticum in northern Phocis, close to modern Amfissa; the straight-line distance from the city of Thebes is about eighty kilometres, but the road has to cross the passes, and there are no large supply points along the way. Sixth, the campaign is dated to the summer of 356 BC; the Third Sacred War broke out with it and did not end until the intervention of Macedon in 346 BC, a matter of roughly ten years. Seventh, on the twenty-first of July of the same year the temple of Artemis at Ephesus burned to the ground, which the Greeks read as a dire omen for the commonwealth of Greece, and it fell in the very year of the Theban victories. As for casualties, neither side has left any figure that can be trusted; all that can be said is that the field army of the Phocian League was practically destroyed, while the losses of Thebes were comparatively light.
cause: 第三次聖戰的直接起因是德爾斐。福基斯長期被指拖欠阿波羅神廟的租金與罰款，安菲克提翁同盟議會在德爾斐召開會議，判定福基斯違規並議決由同盟成員出兵討伐。斐洛梅洛斯率領福基斯民眾攻佔德爾斐主殿，驅走祭司、宣布由福基斯人接管聖地並自行管理，這一舉動等於公開挑戰同盟，把原本的債務糾紛變成一場神聖的義戰，也讓底比斯無法置身事外。底比斯介入同樣帶著政治算盤：科林斯戰爭之後，它是希臘最有力的城邦，藉安菲克提翁同盟的制裁權可以削弱斯巴達在伯羅奔尼撒的同盟網，同時把福基斯各城拉進自己的盟國體系。佩爾狄卡斯與其他底比斯將領態度更強硬，主張不等對方集結就越境打擊，把戰場推到福基斯境內；底比斯面對的難處是分兵與節奏——科林斯戰爭未了，希臘各邦彼此猜忌，底比斯既不能放棄同盟義務，又怕被拖入一場持久消耗戰。於是這場戰爭的起因既是神廟債務，也是城邦霸權的算計。
causeEn: The direct cause of the Third Sacred War lay at Delphi. Phocis had long been accused of falling behind on the rent and the fines owed to the temple of Apollo, and the council of the Amphictyons met at Delphi, pronounced Phocis in violation of the rules, and resolved that the members of the league should take the field against it. Philomelus led the people of Phocis to seize the main temple, drove out the priests, and proclaimed that the sanctuary would be administered by the Phocians themselves. This was an open challenge to the league: it turned what had been a debt dispute into a holy war, and it left Thebes no room to stand aside. Theban intervention carried its own political arithmetic. After the Corinthian War Thebes was the most powerful polis in Greece, and through the sanctioning power of the Amphictyonic League it could weaken Sparta's network of allies in the Peloponnese while pulling the towns of Phocis into its own alliance system. Pelopidas and the other Theban generals took a harder line, arguing for a strike across the border before the enemy could assemble, so as to carry the fighting into Phocis. The difficulty for Thebes was how to split its effort and how to set the pace: the Corinthian War was unfinished, the Greek states distrusted one another, and Thebes could neither abandon its league obligations nor risk being drawn into a war of attrition. The outbreak of this war was therefore at once a temple debt and a calculation of polis hegemony.
impact: 此役之後，底比斯把福基斯西部平原與塞菲索斯河上游的一段置於控制之下，安菲克提翁同盟的實際話語權完全落到它手上，希臘城邦間的均勢再度傾斜；神聖連隊的名聲也在這幾年裡被推到頂點，底比斯最擅長的戰法——以精兵深縱陣加側翼迂迴——成為此後一個多世紀軍事圈的標準命題。然而聖戰並未因此結束：福基斯聯盟被打散的是野戰部隊，聯盟議事會仍在克雷提庫姆一帶運作，斐洛梅洛斯仍以將軍身份主持大局，並在戰後數年裡取得過幾場勝利，直到前354年被刺身亡、俄諾馬科斯接任，才在克羅科斯原與洛里克拉的戰役中連番失利。真正了結第三次聖戰的是馬其頓的腓力二世：他在前352年的克羅科斯原戰役擊潰福基斯聯軍，前346年又接管德爾斐的款項並解散安菲克提翁同盟的武裝，前345年福基斯全境落入腓力之手。換句話說，底比斯用三天贏來的高峰只維持了十來年，就成了腓力二世踏進希臘事務的踏腳石；底比斯在協助同盟擊敗福基斯的同時，也把自己擺到了馬其頓的對面。幾乎所有城邦都在為腓力的介入準備藉口，而那一年以弗所神廟焚毀的凶兆，後來在希臘人回望時，恰好對應底比斯這段短暫而激烈的巔峰。
impactEn: After this battle Thebes brought the western plain of Phocis and a stretch of the upper Cephissus under its control, the real voice of the Amphictyonic League passed entirely to it, and the balance between the Greek city-states tilted once more. The renown of the Sacred Band reached its height in these same years, and the Theban way of fighting, a deep phalanx of picked troops combined with a turning movement against the flank, became a standard proposition in the military writing of the century and more that followed. Yet the sacred war did not end there. What the Phocian League had lost was its field army; its council continued to function in the towns around the Creticum, Philomelus still presided as general, and in the years immediately after the battle he even won several engagements, until his assassination in 354 BC and the accession of Onomarchus, who then suffered defeat after defeat at Crocus Field and at Orchomenus. The war was finally settled by Philip II of Macedon: he broke the Phocian League at the battle of Crocus Field in 352 BC, took over the treasures of Delphi and disarmed the Amphictyonic League in 346 BC, and by 345 BC the whole of Phocis was in his hands. In other words, the peak that Thebes bought with three days of fighting lasted barely a decade before it became a stepping-stone for Philip into Greek affairs; in helping the league crush Phocis, Thebes had also placed itself squarely opposite Macedon. Almost every city-state was already preparing an excuse for Philip's intervention, and the omen of the burning of the temple at Ephesus, recorded that same year, has since seemed to match that brief and violent Theban zenith precisely.
result: 底比斯與聯軍取得完勝。三日之中，福基斯聯盟的野戰部隊在最後一日被突破之後全軍潰散，殘部退入福基斯內陸的山地與城塞，聯盟在平原上的存在被抹去；底比斯人佔領福基斯西部，控制了通往德爾斐的道路與塞菲索斯河上游的渡口，影響力推到福基斯各城。佩爾狄卡斯在戰鬥中腿部受創，包紮之後仍留在營中與將領議事，是這場勝利背後的關鍵人物之一。福基斯一方損失慘重，聯盟議事會在克雷提庫姆一帶重組，斐洛梅洛斯仍留任將軍，並在之後數年以游擊與外交周旋，使聖戰延續了近十年，最後由腓力二世於前346年收拾殘局。從更長的視角看，這場三日之戰是底比斯霸權的頂點而不是終點：底比斯靠它贏得了希臘世界的一步，卻也把自己擺到了馬其頓那頭的對面。而佩爾狄卡斯本人，在這場三日之戰中作為主將得勝之後，仍在前369年率底比斯軍出使泰薩利，最終陣亡於安菲克提翁之戰。
resultEn: Thebes and its coalition won outright. Over the three days the field army of the Phocian League was broken on the last day and dissolved in a rout; the survivors withdrew into the hills and strongholds of the Phocidian interior, and the league's presence in the plain was wiped out. The Thebans occupied western Phocis, controlled the road to Delphi and the crossings of the upper Cephissus, and extended their influence over the towns of the country. Pelopidas was wounded in the leg during the fighting and, once the wound was dressed, stayed in camp to confer with the generals; he was one of the men behind the victory. The Phocian side paid heavily, the league council reconstituted itself around the Creticum, Philomelus remained general, and for the following years he kept the war alive by raids and diplomacy, so that the sacred war dragged on for close to another decade before Philip II settled it in 346 BC. Seen in the longer perspective, this three-day battle was the summit rather than the end of Theban hegemony: with it Thebes took a step forward in the Greek world, and at the same time set itself directly opposite Macedon. Pelopidas himself, having commanded the winning side in this three-day battle, led a Theban army into Thessaly in 369 BC and was killed in the fighting of the Amphictyonic war.
